title: The study of the circumnuclear environment of accreting supermassive black holes with realistic X-ray spectral models
comment: 18 pages, 9 figures, the models are available: https://www.astro.unige.ch/reflex/xspec-models
summary: X-ray spectral modeling is a powerful tool for studying the immediate environment of accreting objects, including supermassive black holes. Several models, either phenomenological or physically driven, have been developed over the past decade to study X-ray spectra, delivering important insights into the properties of circumnuclear material of active galactic nuclei (AGN). Despite the fact that these models are able to reproduce the data well, they often lack realistic geometries, and most of them consist of simplified configurations such as a slab or a torus. We use the ray-tracing code \textsc{RefleX} to generate new spectral models that cover a wide energy range in the X-ray band, adopting a realistic configuration for the surrounding material. We introduce two new table models that are publicly available: 1) the RXToPo model, which features an X-ray source along with a dusty torus and a polar hollow cone; 2) the RXagn1 model, which includes, besides the torus and polar cone, also the accretion disk and the broad line region. Both models were applied to the X-ray spectrum of NGC 424, demonstrating their potential to study sources whose X-ray emission is dominated by reprocessed radiation.

AI.tldr: New realistic X-ray spectral models using ray-tracing (RefleX) better represent AGN environments and successfully analyze the spectrum of NGC 424.
AI.motivation: Current X-ray spectral models for accreting supermassive black holes have unrealistic geometries, limiting detailed understanding of circumnuclear material.
AI.method: Used the ray-tracing code RefleX to create new spectral models with realistic surrounding material configurations, including dusty torus, polar hollow cone, accretion disk, and broad line region.
AI.result: Developed two public table models, RXToPo and RXagn1, capable of covering a wide X-ray energy range and applied them successfully to the X-ray spectrum of NGC 424, highlighting their effectiveness.
AI.conclusion: The new models improve the realism of X-ray spectral modeling, enabling better study of AGN environments where X-ray emission is dominated by reprocessed radiation.

title: X-ray spectroscopy mass constraints on V1674 Her: the fastest nova does not have a near-Chandrasekhar white dwarf
summary: V1674 Her (Nova Her 2021) is the fastest classical nova ever recorded, with an optical decline time of $t_2 \sim 1$ day, typically interpreted as evidence for a white dwarf mass close to the Chandrasekhar limit. We present a broadband X-ray study of V1674 Her combining contemporaneous XMM-Newton and NuSTAR observations in quiescence to directly constrain the white dwarf mass and magnetic field strength. The hard X-ray emission is modeled using a physically motivated post-shock accretion column model that accounts for the temperature gradient in the flow and reflection from the white dwarf surface. Under the assumption that the accretion disk is truncated at the co-rotation radius, we obtain a white dwarf mass of $M = 1.09^{+0.07}_{-0.06}\,M_\odot$. An independent constraint derived from timing analysis of the X-ray power spectrum yields a consistent value of $M = 1.12 \pm 0.06\,M_\odot$. These values are significantly lower than those inferred from empirical decline-time relations, suggesting that such relations may overestimate white dwarf masses in extreme fast novae. From the inferred accretion rate and magnetospheric radius, we estimate a surface magnetic field strength of $B = 21.3^{+6.6}_{-5.7}\,(\mathrm{stat})^{+12.9}_{-8.1}\,(\mathrm{sys})\,\mathrm{MG}$, placing V1674 Her at the high end of the magnetic field distribution for intermediate polars. Our results demonstrate that even the fastest novae do not necessarily host near-Chandrasekhar white dwarfs, highlighting the importance of direct X-ray constraints and suggesting that additional parameters beyond white dwarf mass play a key role in setting nova timescales.

AI.tldr: Broadband X-ray observations of the fastest classical nova V1674 Her reveal its white dwarf mass is around 1.1 solar masses, less than previous estimates based on optical decline times, and it possesses a strong magnetic field, indicating factors beyond mass drive nova speed.
AI.motivation: V1674 Her is the fastest recorded classical nova, with an extremely rapid optical decline time, typically linked to white dwarfs near the Chandrasekhar mass limit. The motivation is to directly constrain the white dwarf's mass and magnetic field using X-ray observations to test this assumption.
AI.method: The study uses contemporaneous XMM-Newton and NuSTAR X-ray observations in quiescence, modeling the hard X-ray emission with a post-shock accretion column model that incorporates temperature gradients and reflection. Timing analysis of the X-ray power spectrum provides an independent mass constraint.
AI.result: The white dwarf mass was constrained to about 1.09–1.12 solar masses, significantly below the Chandrasekhar limit and lower than masses inferred from empirical decline-time relations. The surface magnetic field strength is estimated to be approximately 21 MG, placing V1674 Her among highly magnetic intermediate polars.
AI.conclusion: Empirical relations using optical decline times may overestimate white dwarf masses in extremely fast novae. Direct X-ray constraints reveal that even the fastest novae do not necessarily harbor near-Chandrasekhar white dwarfs, implying other parameters besides mass influence nova speed.

title: Nuclear Constraints on $^{12}$C$(α,γ)^{16}$O and Their Impact on Black-Hole Mass Predictions
summary:
Gravitational-wave observations have renewed interest in the black-hole mass gap and in the maximum mass of first-generation black holes below its lower edge. The \(^{12}{\rm C}(α,γ)^{16}{\rm O}\) reaction plays a central role in this problem because it determines the carbon-to-oxygen ratio after core-helium burning and thereby affects the later evolution of massive stars toward pulsational pair instability and pair-instability supernovae.
  Recent attempts to constrain \(S(300~{\rm keV})\) from gravitational-wave population inferences face important limitations, because the lower edge of the black-hole mass gap is not directly measured. It is inferred model dependently from assumptions about stellar evolution, metallicity, mass loss, rotation, binary evolution, hierarchical mergers, selection effects, priors, and the adopted population model. Therefore, values of \(S(300~{\rm keV})\) inferred from black-hole populations must remain consistent with independent nuclear-physics constraints.
  In this work we reanalyze the low-energy \(^{12}{\rm C}(α,γ)^{16}{\rm O}\) \(S\) factor using updated information on the subthreshold \(1^{-}\) and \(2^{+}\) ANCs and on the ground-state ANC of \(^{16}{\rm O}\), together with direct capture data. These constraints favor a lower \(S(300~{\rm keV})\) than the older central evaluation and disfavor very large values required by some black-hole-population interpretations. Using the resulting ANC-constrained \(S(300~{\rm keV})\) range and the transformed relation between this quantity and the lower edge of the pair-instability mass gap, we estimate \[ \frac{M_{\rm BH}}{M_\odot}\simeq 61\text{--}75 . \] Thus, the present nuclear-physics constraints favor a relatively high lower edge of the first-generation black-hole mass gap.

AI.tldr: This paper refines the key nuclear reaction rate influencing massive star evolution using updated nuclear data, which leads to a higher estimate of the lower edge of the black-hole mass gap around 61-75 solar masses, challenging some gravitational-wave-based population inferences.
AI.motivation: To address uncertainties in the black-hole mass gap lower edge determination related to the nuclear reaction rate of the carbon-oxygen ratio after core-helium burning in massive stars.
AI.method: Reanalysis of the low-energy 12C(α,γ)16O S factor using updated asymptotic normalization coefficients (ANCs) and direct capture data to refine nuclear physics input relevant to stellar evolution.
AI.result: The updated ANC-constrained S(300 keV) favors lower values than previous evaluations, disfavoring very large rates required by some black-hole population models, and implies a higher lower edge of the first-generation black-hole mass gap at approximately 61-75 solar masses.
AI.conclusion: Nuclear-physics constraints from updated S factor analyses impose a relatively high lower edge of the black-hole mass gap, limiting interpretations from gravitational-wave black-hole populations that require large S factor values inconsistent with these constraints.

title: Anisotropic Thermal Conduction as a Driver of Jet Collimation and Magnetic Field Amplification on Cold Fronts
summary: Galaxy clusters contain a hot, diffuse, and weakly magnetized plasma known as the intracluster medium (ICM). In this environment, how thermal conduction influences plasma dynamics and the conditions under which it operates efficiently remain open questions in cluster physics. Systems in which active galactic nuclei (AGN) jets interact with cold fronts produced by cluster mergers provide a unique setting to examine the interplay between conduction, jet dynamics, and ordered magnetic fields. To interpret the detailed structures revealed by recent observations, it is therefore important, as a first theoretical step, to quantify how thermal conduction modifies AGN jet morphology and the surrounding magnetic-field configuration. We perform two-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations of an AGN jet in an ICM environment, incorporating anisotropic thermal conduction with varying efficiency. The simulations show that thermal conduction transports heat from the jet head backward along magnetic field lines into the inner cocoon. This process increases the inner cocoon pressure, enhancing jet collimation by a factor of $\sim 4$ compared to models without conduction. This stronger collimation stretches the magnetic fields along the cold-front surface, resulting in a maximum field strength up to a factor of $\sim 1.5$ larger. Jet collimation increases as the conduction efficiency increases, which is interpreted as a conductive collimation mechanism. These results suggest that anisotropic thermal conduction can operate effectively on jet scales in galaxy clusters, and that accounting for conduction may be important when interpreting jet morphology and magnetic field structure in merging cluster environments.

AI.tldr: MHD simulations demonstrate that anisotropic thermal conduction in galaxy clusters enhances AGN jet collimation and strengthens magnetic fields by transporting heat along field lines, suggesting conduction is a key factor in shaping jet and magnetic field structures in merging cluster environments.
AI.motivation: To understand how thermal conduction affects plasma dynamics, specifically AGN jet morphology and magnetic field structure in galaxy clusters, especially where jets interact with cold fronts from cluster mergers.
AI.method: Two-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations of AGN jets in an intracluster medium (ICM) were performed, incorporating varying efficiencies of anisotropic thermal conduction.
AI.result: Thermal conduction transports heat along magnetic field lines from the jet head to the inner cocoon, raising inner cocoon pressure and enhancing jet collimation by about a factor of 4, while magnetic fields along cold fronts are strengthened by up to a factor of 1.5. Increased conduction efficiency correlates with stronger jet collimation.
AI.conclusion: Anisotropic thermal conduction significantly influences AGN jet morphology by enhancing jet collimation and altering the magnetic field configuration in galaxy cluster environments.

title: Dark siren cross-correlations and the sensitivity of $H_0$ to methodological choices
summary: Gravitational wave sources act as absolute distance indicators, making them powerful probes of the present-day expansion rate of the Universe, $H_0$. The cross-correlation method combines gravitational wave events with galaxy catalogues to constrain cosmological parameters through their shared large-scale structure. In this work, we investigate how key methodological choices -- including covariance treatment, bias parametrisation for galaxies and gravitational wave events, and distance and redshift binning width -- affect the inferred value of $H_0$. We also study catalogue incompleteness, showing that selection effects can be incorporated directly into the theoretical prediction, without the need to model the missing population explicitly, a key advantage over the standard galaxy catalogue approach. Our results indicate that, with appropriate modelling choices and a sufficiently large sample of precise gravitational wave events, the systematic biases considered here can be effectively mitigated, highlighting the potential of the cross-correlation method for future dark siren precision cosmology.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how methodological factors affect measuring the Hubble constant using gravitational wave events and galaxy catalogues, showing that careful modelling can reduce biases and improve future cosmological constraints from dark sirens.
AI.motivation: To explore how methodological choices influence the estimation of the Hubble constant ($H_0$) using gravitational wave events and galaxy catalogues, addressing limitations in current approaches.
AI.method: Investigates the impact of covariance treatment, bias parametrisation, distance and redshift binning, and catalogue incompleteness on $H_0$ inference using the cross-correlation method combining gravitational wave sources and galaxy catalogues; incorporates selection effects into theoretical predictions.
AI.result: Finds that with proper modelling and a large sample of precise gravitational wave events, systematic biases from methodological choices can be mitigated, enhancing the reliability of $H_0$ measurements.
AI.conclusion: The cross-correlation method, when carefully applied with consideration of key methodological factors and catalogue selection effects, holds significant promise for accurate and precise measurements of the Universe's expansion rate using gravitational wave data.

title: Resonant Inverse Compton Scattering and Hard X-ray Emission in Magnetar Magnetospheres
summary: Magnetars are a subclass of neutron stars with ultra-strong surface magnetic fields. Some magnetars exhibit persistent hard X-ray emission, characterized by power-law tails with photon indices around 1--1.5, extending from ${\sim}$10 keV to several hundred keV. The leading explanation for this hard X-ray component is resonant Compton scattering, in which the thermal seed photons are upscattered by relativistic electron-positron pairs flowing along magnetic field lines in the magnetosphere. In this work, we adopt the pair outflow framework of the magnetar magnetosphere and calculate the resonant Compton scattering opacity, as well as the spectrum and polarization of the upscattered emission. We find that resonant cooling can substantially modify the magnetospheric plasma density and impose strong optical depth constraints on the hard X-ray emission regions. Under the viewing geometry inferred from IXPE, an equatorial twist near the stellar surface provides a viable configuration for the NuSTAR hard X-ray spectrum of 4U 0142+61, while a polar-twist geometry is disfavored. Joint spectral, timing, and polarimetric modeling will be essential for distinguishing between the magnetospheric scattering geometries and understanding the physical properties of the pair plasma.

AI.tldr: This paper models resonant Compton scattering in magnetar magnetospheres to explain hard X-ray emission, finding that viewing geometry affects observed spectra and polarization, with equatorial twists favored over polar twists for 4U 0142+61.
AI.motivation: To understand the origin and characteristics of the persistent hard X-ray emission observed in magnetars, particularly the resonant Compton scattering process in their magnetospheres.
AI.method: Adopting the pair outflow framework of the magnetar magnetosphere, calculating the resonant Compton scattering opacity, and modeling the spectrum and polarization of the upscattered emission under different geometries.
AI.result: Resonant cooling significantly alters the magnetospheric plasma density and imposes strong constraints on the optical depth of hard X-ray emission regions. The model favors an equatorial twist near the stellar surface for explaining the observed NuSTAR spectrum of 4U 0142+61, while a polar-twist geometry is less favored.
AI.conclusion: Joint spectral, timing, and polarimetric analysis is critical to differentiate between scattering geometries in the magnetar magnetosphere and to better understand the pair plasma's physical properties.

title: On the origin of the environmental step: A BayeSN view of the ZTF SN Ia DR2
comment: 13 pages, 13 figures, 7 tables. Submitted to MNRAS
summary: Astrophysical variabilities of Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia), such as their link with their birth environment, are now one of the leading sources of systematic uncertainties on the measurement of the dark energy equation-of-state parameter $w$. Population studies of SNe Ia, using large samples, give precious insights into these variabilities. We analyse a volume-limited subsample of the ZTF SN Ia DR2 with BayeSN, a hierarchical Bayesian model for SN Ia SEDs. We investigate the distributions of SN Ia light curve parameters and their link with SN environment. Using a new training of BayeSN released in a companion paper, we find a smaller scatter of Hubble residuals compared to SALT. We then investigate the magnitude step, which accounts for the correlation between SN Ia standardised absolute magnitude and host environments. We find a posteriori steps of $0.103\pm0.010$ mag (a $10.1σ$ difference from 0) when using global stellar mass as an environmental proxy, and $0.086\pm0.010$ mag ($8.3σ$) when using local colour, in accordance with steps computed using SALT light curve fits. This confirms that the large step seen in the ZTF SN Ia DR2 data was not due to the SALT fit or the associated standardisation process. We then investigate the origin of the step, using a BayeSN model which accounts for both an intrinsic magnitude step and differing dust properties with the SN environment. We find a $0.103\pm0.018$ mag ($5.6σ$) step in global mass and a $0.085\pm0.019$ mag ($4.5σ$) step in local colour. The means of the $R_V$ distribution are similar between different host environments, with $Δ\mathbb{E}(R_V)\leq0.2$ across all environment proxies, with significances ranging from $0.6σ$ to $1.2σ$. This is a strong signal of the existence of an intrinsic dependence of SN Ia absolute magnitude on environment.

AI.tldr: This paper uses a Bayesian model to analyze Type Ia supernova data, confirming that their absolute magnitude depends intrinsically on their host environment, which impacts dark energy measurements, independent of dust and light curve fitting methods.
AI.motivation: To understand astrophysical variabilities of Type Ia supernovae linked to birth environment that cause systematic uncertainties in dark energy equation-of-state parameter measurements, and to clarify the origin of observed magnitude steps related to SN Ia host environment.
AI.method: The authors applied the hierarchical Bayesian model BayeSN to a volume-limited subsample of the ZTF SN Ia DR2, analyzing light curve parameters and environmental correlations. They compared results with SALT fits, used environmental proxies (global stellar mass, local color), and incorporated intrinsic magnitude steps and dust property variations into their model.
AI.result: They found reduced scatter in Hubble residuals with BayeSN compared to SALT, confirmed significant magnitude steps correlated with global stellar mass and local color, and detected no substantial variation in dust law parameters (R_V) across environments, reinforcing the presence of intrinsic magnitude-environment dependency.
AI.conclusion: The study concludes there is a significant intrinsic dependence of Type Ia supernova absolute magnitude on their host environment, independent of the light curve fitting method used, supported by measured magnitude steps correlated with global stellar mass and local color of host galaxies.

title: Diffuse gamma-ray emissions around the stellar cluster Berkeley 59
summary: We report a detailed analysis on the young stellar cluster Berkeley 59 using Fermi-LAT. Using up-to-date source catalog and background models, we found significant extended GeV emission around Berkeley 59, which can be modeled by a radial disk of 1.02 degree radius with a significance of the extension of 10.6 sigma. We investigated the molecular, neutral and ionized gas content and the hadronic origin. The gamma-ray spectrum of Berkeley 59 has a photon index of 2.88. The derived gas mass from H2 and HII around Berkeley 59 is about 289 solar mass. We derived the relationship between cosmic ray acceleration efficiency and diffusion coefficient. Our results suggest that the extended gamma-ray emission originates from cosmic rays accelerated by cluster winds interacting with surrounding gas.

AI.tldr: Fermi-LAT observations reveal significant extended gamma-ray emission around Berkeley 59, linked to cosmic rays accelerated by cluster winds interacting with surrounding gas.
AI.motivation: To analyze the young stellar cluster Berkeley 59 for gamma-ray emissions and understand their origin.
AI.method: Used Fermi-LAT data with updated source catalog and background models to detect and model extended GeV emission; investigated molecular, neutral and ionized gas content; analyzed hadronic origin and derived cosmic ray acceleration efficiency and diffusion coefficient.
AI.result: Detected significant extended GeV emission around Berkeley 59 modeled by a 1.02 degree radius radial disk with 10.6 sigma significance; gamma-ray spectrum photon index of 2.88; gas mass around Berkeley 59 about 289 solar masses; suggested gamma rays originate from cosmic rays accelerated by cluster winds interacting with surrounding gas.
AI.conclusion: The extended gamma-ray emission observed around Berkeley 59 is caused by cosmic rays accelerated by cluster winds interacting with the ambient gas, supported by the spectral and spatial analysis and gas content measurements.

title: CMB Limits on the Absorption of Light Vector and Axial-Vector Dark Matter
summary: Leptophilic sub-MeV spin-1 dark matter (DM) can be converted into a photon via inelastic scattering with a free electron or absorption by a neutral hydrogen atom in the primordial plasma. We study for the first time the impact of the energy injection resulting from such processes on cosmic microwave background (CMB) anisotropies. We obtain upper limits on the vector and axial-vector DM-electron couplings using Planck 2018 temperature, polarization, and lensing data for DM masses between 100 eV and 100 keV. We find that, due to the suppression of the hydrogen atomic form factor at high energies, inelastic scattering provides the dominant constraint for DM masses above the keV scale. At lower masses, hydrogen ionization through DM absorption is the leading channel, driven by the higher efficiency of post-recombination energy injection in modifying the free-electron fraction. Although the bounds we derive are considerably weaker than existing laboratory and astrophysical limits, they provide a robust and independent cosmological probe of leptophilic DM interactions.

AI.tldr: This study constrains leptophilic sub-MeV spin-1 dark matter couplings by analyzing energy injection effects on the CMB, revealing mass-dependent dominant interaction channels and providing an independent cosmological probe complementary to other limits.
AI.motivation: Investigate the impact of leptophilic sub-MeV spin-1 dark matter interactions on the cosmic microwave background (CMB) anisotropies, exploring an independent cosmological probe of such dark matter properties.
AI.method: Analyze energy injection into the primordial plasma caused by inelastic scattering of dark matter with free electrons and absorption by neutral hydrogen, and constrain dark matter-electron couplings using Planck 2018 CMB temperature, polarization, and lensing data for a mass range of 100 eV to 100 keV.
AI.result: Obtained upper limits on vector and axial-vector dark matter-electron couplings; found inelastic scattering dominates constraints above keV scales due to atomic form factor suppression; below keV, absorption-driven hydrogen ionization is dominant, affecting the free-electron fraction post-recombination.
AI.conclusion: CMB anisotropies provide a robust, independent cosmological constraint on leptophilic sub-MeV spin-1 dark matter interactions, complementing existing laboratory and astrophysical limits despite weaker bounds.

title: KM3-230213A and potential astrophysical sources
comment: Contribution to the 2026 Very High Energy Phenomena in the Universe session of the 60th Rencontres de Moriond
summary: The recent detection of the ultra-high energy neutrino KM3-230213A by KM3NeT/ARCA marks the first observation of an astrophysical neutrino with energy above 100 PeV, opening a new window to the ultra-high energy Universe. In this contribution, the current global ultra-high energy neutrino landscape in light of this event is reviewed, including tension of this observation with existing limits set by the IceCube and the Pierre Auger Observatories. Different scenarios are discussed to explain its origin. Recent efforts to constrain features of potential source populations using the inferred diffuse ultra-high energy neutrino flux are also presented.

AI.tldr: The detection of a neutrino above 100 PeV by KM3NeT/ARCA introduces new insights into ultra-high energy neutrinos, reveals tensions with previous observatory limits, and informs source population models through diffuse flux analysis.
AI.motivation: To explore the implications of the first detection of an astrophysical neutrino above 100 PeV by KM3NeT/ARCA and its impact on understanding the ultra-high energy Universe.
AI.method: Reviewing the current global ultra-high energy neutrino landscape, analyzing the tension between this observation and existing limits from IceCube and Pierre Auger Observatories, and discussing scenarios explaining the neutrino's origin, along with recent efforts to constrain source population features using the diffuse neutrino flux.
AI.result: Identification of a new energy range for astrophysical neutrinos, highlighting inconsistencies with prior observatory limits and providing insights into potential source populations through diffuse flux constraints.
AI.conclusion: The detection of KM3-230213A opens a novel observational window into ultra-high energy neutrinos, challenges existing limits, and advances understanding of their astrophysical origins and source characteristics.

title: Advance warning of $γ$-ray blazar flares from \textit{Fermi}-LAT light curves: a strictly causal machine-learning backtest
summary: Long-term \textit{Fermi}-LAT monitoring makes it possible to ask whether a blazar light curve shows signs of an upcoming flare before the flare becomes obvious in the $γ$-ray emission. We present a strictly causal machine-learning framework for forecasting $γ$-ray blazar flares from 3-d binned LAT light curves. Flare intervals are identified with Bayesian Blocks, and each light curve is sampled with 365-d trailing windows from which 42 variability features are measured. We train separate WATCH and TRIGGER models: WATCH predicts whether flare activity will appear within the next 90 d, while TRIGGER predicts whether a new flare onset will occur within the next 45 d. To avoid temporal leakage, all scaling, calibration, threshold selection, and validation use only the pre-cutoff data before MJD 60000. We apply the method to the FSRQ 4FGL\,J1048.4$+$7143, using 13 bright blazars as auxiliary training sources. Among logistic regression, polynomial logistic regression, and random forest classifiers, polynomial logistic regression gives the strongest held-out WATCH performance, with ROC AUC $=0.891$, average precision $=0.396$, and a block-permutation probability $p_{\rm perm}=0.006$. At the selected WATCH threshold, it recovers 18 of the 21 positive windows in the held-out WATCH set, corresponding to a recall of 0.86. The same model also gives the best held-out TRIGGER ranking, with TRIGGER AUC $=0.770$ and TRIGGER AP $=0.123$, although no reliable pre-onset TRIGGER alert is obtained. The WATCH state appears before both held-out flare episodes, with final alerts 4.5 and 2.5 d before onset. The corresponding broader WATCH-active periods begin 88.5 and 72.5 d before flare onset. These results suggest that long-term {\fermi} light curves contain useful predictive information about the build-up to blazar flares.

AI.tldr: A machine-learning framework using Fermi-LAT gamma-ray light curves can predict blazar flares weeks before they occur, with polynomial logistic regression models showing strong predictive ability and offering earlier alerts for flare activity.
AI.motivation: To determine if upcoming gamma-ray blazar flares can be predicted before becoming obvious in the emission, enabling earlier alerts and understanding of flare dynamics.
AI.method: Bayesian Blocks identify flare intervals in 3-day binned light curves; 365-day trailing windows extract 42 variability features; logistic regression and random forest classifiers are trained to predict flare occurrences within 45 and 90 days, using pre-cutoff data to avoid temporal leakage.
AI.result: Polynomial logistic regression achieved the best performance with WATCH model ROC AUC of 0.891 and recall of 0.86, successfully predicting flare activity within 90 days and giving alerts days before flare onset, confirming the presence of useful predictive features in the data.
AI.conclusion: Long-term Fermi-LAT light curves contain predictive information that can forecast the build-up to blazar gamma-ray flares several weeks in advance using machine learning models.

title: Young Massive Star Clusters as TeV Emitters: Constraints from H.E.S.S. and LHAASO
comment: Accepted for publication in A&A 07 May 2026
summary: Young massive star clusters (YMSCs) have been proposed as excellent candidates for the main sources of Galactic cosmic rays (CRs) up to the PeV range. The detection and study of gamma rays in the very-high-energy (E>100GeV) range has brought arguments in favour of this hypothesis. Current instruments have detected only a few YMSCs. Future observatories are expected to increase this number, providing a larger sample improving our ability to constrain the role of YMSCs in the origin of CRs. We study the population of TeV YMSCs detected and their properties, confronting simulations of the YMSC population to the observed sample, to address the fundamental questions concerning the spectrum of accelerated particles, the efficiency of CR production, and the fraction of the wind luminosity converted into turbulent magnetic fields. Using Monte Carlo methods, we simulate the Galactic population of YMSCs in the gamma-ray domain and confront our simulations to the catalogue of sources of the systematic survey of the Galactic plane performed by H.E.S.S. (HGPS) and the First LHAASO Catalogue of Gamma-Ray Sources. We systematically explore the parameter space of our model, including the slope of accelerated particles $α$, the CR efficiency $η_{\rm CR}$, the fraction of the wind luminosity converted into turbulent magnetic field $η_{\rm b}$, and the diffusion regime. We found 5 possible sets of parameters for which >75% of realisations agree with the combined data from the HGPS and LHAASO 1st catalogue. Certain regions of the parameter space are strongly disfavoured, such as Bohm diffusion. Our model successfully reproduces the YMSC population observed in both catalogues. With future systematic surveys, e.g. the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO), this approach will help break degeneracies and improve our understanding of particle acceleration at YMSC shocks in the Galaxy.

AI.tldr: This paper uses Monte Carlo simulations to model young massive star clusters as sources of Galactic cosmic rays, matching simulated outputs to gamma-ray observations and constraining key physical parameters, supporting YMSCs' role in cosmic ray origin and guiding future observations.
AI.motivation: Young massive star clusters are proposed as major sources of Galactic cosmic rays up to PeV energies, but current observations are limited and the physical parameters governing cosmic ray production are uncertain.
AI.method: Using Monte Carlo simulations of the Galactic YMSC population in gamma rays, the study compared simulated populations to observed TeV gamma-ray sources from H.E.S.S. and LHAASO catalogues, systematically exploring model parameters including particle acceleration slope, cosmic ray efficiency, magnetic field conversion fraction, and diffusion regime.
AI.result: The study identified five parameter sets that align well (>75% agreement) with observed data, ruling out some diffusion regimes like Bohm diffusion, and successfully reproducing the observed YMSC population at TeV energies.
AI.conclusion: Modeling and comparison to gamma-ray surveys supports YMSCs as significant contributors to Galactic cosmic rays, and future observatories like CTAO will improve constraints on particle acceleration and cosmic ray production mechanisms in these clusters.

title: Detection of persistent helium absorption in the 91bg-like type Ia Supernova 2022an
comment: Submitted to the AAS journal. Comments are welcome
summary: We present optical and near-infrared observations of the fast-declining Type Ia supernova (SN Ia) 2022an. The photometric and spectroscopic properties identify it as a standard 91bg-like event; however, our data reveal a relatively narrow absorption feature with a full width at half maximum (FWHM) of 75 angstroms near $1.037\,μ$m in the rest frame of the observed spectra that persists from around 30 days to nearly 90 days after maximum light. We attribute this feature to He I $1.083\,μ$m line with a blueshifted velocity of $1.3\times10^{4}$ km s$^{-1}$ and a FWHM of $2.1\times10^{3}$ km s$^{-1}$, supported by the detection of multiple optical He I transitions in earlier epochs at a higher velocity around $1.5\times10^{4}$ km s$^{-1}$. The high velocity of the helium could not be explained by helium external to the progenitor at the explosion, such as the stripped surface helium from a companion star. The properties of the helium absorption in SN 2022an spectra instead point to unburnt material in the outer ejecta, thus providing the most compelling evidence to date for helium-bearing ejecta in a 91bg-like SN Ia. Such helium has been predicted for sub-Chandrasekhar-mass double-detonation explosions involving a surface helium shell. No theoretical calculations of modern helium-shell double detonation have been performed at epochs similar to those observed for SN 2022an to study the effect of helium on their spectra, revealing a gap between observations and theoretical calculations in understanding the manifestation of helium in SNe Ia. Nevertheless, the discovery of persistent helium absorption in SN 2022an demonstrates the diagnostic power of NIR spectroscopy for understanding thermonuclear supernova explosions by probing the abundance and structure of their ejecta.

AI.tldr: We observed helium absorption in the near-infrared spectra of SN 2022an, a fast-declining 91bg-like Type Ia supernova, indicating unburnt helium in the outer ejecta from a likely sub-Chandrasekhar-mass double-detonation explosion; this discovery bridges observational evidence and theoretical modeling gaps and underscores the importance of NIR spectroscopy in supernova studies.
AI.motivation: To investigate the presence and origin of helium in a fast-declining 91bg-like Type Ia supernova, addressing the gap between observations and theoretical models of helium-shell double detonations.
AI.method: Optical and near-infrared photometric and spectroscopic observations of SN 2022an, focusing on the identification and analysis of absorption features, particularly a narrow helium absorption line and its velocity characteristics over time.
AI.result: Detection of a persistent narrow helium absorption feature near 1.037 µm with blueshifted velocities incompatible with external helium sources, indicating unburnt helium in the outer ejecta consistent with sub-Chandrasekhar-mass double-detonation models; highlighted the lack of theoretical calculations at observed epochs.
AI.conclusion: The study provides compelling evidence for helium-bearing ejecta in a 91bg-like SN Ia, showing that near-infrared spectroscopy is a powerful diagnostic tool to probe ejecta composition and structure in thermonuclear supernovae, while revealing the need for updated theoretical models of helium-shell double detonations at relevant epochs.

title: Magnetar field dynamics driven by chiral anomalies without magnetic helicity
comment: 16 pages, 9 figures. Submitted for publication. Comments are welcome
summary: The chiral magnetic effect (CME), arising from the chiral anomaly and enabling a mutual conversion between magnetic topology and fermionic chirality, is a key mechanism in magnetar field evolution. Previous work by Dehman & Pons (2025) demonstrated that the CME can efficiently generate dipolar fields ($B_{\rm dip} \gtrsim 10^{14}~\mathrm{G}$), consistent with magnetar timing measurements, provided that the initial magnetic field carries net helicity. However, whether neutron stars are born with magnetic helicity remains uncertain. In this work, we investigate the CME across a range of initial helicity configurations, including non-helical initial conditions. We find that the CME efficiently generates magnetar-strength dipoles on timescales of decades, independently of the initial helicity content. The instability is driven by localized helical structures that induce a residual chiral asymmetry and is primarily governed by the maximum chiral chemical potential, requiring $μ_5^{\rm max} \gtrsim \mathrm{few}\times10^{-11}~\mathrm{MeV}$ for onset in the magnetar regime. Our results further show that these dipoles may either remain stable and subsequently evolve through standard Ohmic decay, or become unstable if they acquire sufficient helicity, in which case they decay through the chiral anomaly, transferring energy to less helical modes. This outcome depends sensitively on the initial helicity distribution. These findings extend the applicability of the CME to more realistic magnetic-field configurations and underscore the importance of the helicity distribution at birth, a quantity that remains poorly constrained in neutron star formation, yet is crucial for determining neutron star magnetic evolution and magnetar formation.
